administration.subject: Social Studies
administration.textAvailabilityWarning: This is the central finding for the redesign era. TEA states: 'Since STAAR is now an online assessment with technology enhanced items, PDF versions of STAAR released tests are no longer available.' For 2023, 2024, and 2025, TEA publishes the answer key, the item rationale, and the student-expectations-tested table for all 40 items, but publishes ITEM TEXT only for the non-multiple-choice items, which are reproduced in an Appendix to the answer key and in the constructed-response scoring guides. Every multiple-choice item from 2023 to 2025 is therefore metadata-only: we know its position, item type, TEA's TEKS label, reporting category, readiness/supporting designation, and official key, but not its stem or options. Those items are recorded in ../item-index.json and cannot be captured here.

capture.scope: Every redesign-era item that (a) TEA published text for AND (b) is tagged to one of the 23 Boston chapter SEs.
capture.method: Item text transcribed from the Appendix of TEA's answer-key PDFs, from TEA's constructed-response scoring guides, and from the 2023 paper item sampler. Correct answers taken from TEA's official key tables.
capture.transcriptionNote: The 2023 and 2024 answer-key appendices are PDFs whose text layer contains character overprinting and OCR artifacts (for example 'Bcsed' for 'Based', and doubled letters throughout). Obvious artifacts of that kind were corrected during transcription. Any text that could not be recovered with confidence is set to null and flagged, never guessed.
capture.optionPoolWarning: For several drag-and-drop items TEA's appendix shows only the CORRECT placements, not the full pool of draggable options, and the prompt says 'Not all answers will be used'. Those items carry optionPoolComplete: false. Do not treat their option list as the full item.

items.teksClause: Covers four of the six named 8.4(A) clauses in one item: the Proclamation of 1763, the Stamp Act, lack of representation in Parliament, and British economic policies following the French and Indian War.
items.prompt:
Select TWO of the following issues. How was each issue a cause of the American Revolution?
• Proclamation of 1763
• The Stamp Act
• Lack of representation in Parliament
• British economic policies following the French and Indian War
Think about the question carefully. Then enter your answer in the box provided.

scorePoints.description: Score two points for correct answers that include references to any two:

Proclamation of 1763: The British restricted/prevented westward expansion and settlement.
Stamp Act: All colonists had to pay taxes on documents and paper.
Taxes had to be paid in silver, which was difficult to acquire.
Unfair taxation/lack of representation i: Colonists had to pay taxes that were created by a government in which they did not have representation.
British economic policies following the: The British used taxes from the colonies to pay off debt from the war.

scorePoints.description: The response provides only half of the correct details.
The response is incorrect or irrelevant.

items.whyThisMatters: This is the single most valuable released item found for this repo. It is an official TEA free-response item on 8.4(A) with an official rubric, and it covers three of Boston mission one's concepts directly: the Stamp Act's scope on documents and paper, taxation without representation, and postwar British debt policy. It is also the only released item that matches the boss-duel format, which is free response graded against pre-authored acceptable answers. TEA's own rubric bullets are a ready-made acceptable-answer set for that grader. Note also the second Stamp Act bullet, 'Taxes had to be paid in silver, which was difficult to acquire' — TEA treats the hard-coin problem as acceptable content, which is exactly the HARD_COIN_SCARCITY micro-concept the repo already has.
items.scoredStudentResponses: 12 real, TEA-scored student responses for this item are captured in ../eval/scr-8.4A-2023-scored-student-responses.json.

Membership in the Council and . . . in the Assembly . . . was composed . . . both of members elected by the people and of members of the Council appointed by the authorities in England . . . .

provenance.correctAnswerFromOfficialKey: Thomas Jefferson: Summarized the reasons for breaking away from Britain in the Declaration of Independence; George Washington: Led the Continental Army in key victories against the British; Thomas Paine: Wrote ideas in the pamphlet Common Sense that inspired colonists to support the revolution; Crispus Attucks: Became the first casualty of the American Revolution when he was killed at the Boston Massacre
provenance.provenanceCaveat: IMPORTANT. This is a SAMPLE test question, not a released test form item. TEA distinguishes the two: 'A test form is a set of released test questions previously administered together to Texas students... Sample test questions are small subsets of test questions released from the STAAR test banks. These test questions MAY HAVE BEEN previously administered.' So unlike every other item in content/staar, we CANNOT assert that this item was administered to Texas students. It is genuinely published by TEA and genuinely keyed by TEA; it is not confirmed to be an operational item.

items.whyThisMatters: This is the ONLY TEA-published item found for 8.4(B) across seven summative administrations plus the sampler. 8.4(B) is otherwise a total gap. It names Crispus Attucks and the Boston Massacre, which is Boston mission M6, and George Washington, which supports mission M14. Its weaker provenance (sampler, not confirmed administered) is exactly why it is tagged provenanceStrength SAMPLER_NOT_CONFIRMED_ADMINISTERED rather than being silently mixed in with the form items.

notCapturedButPublished.reason: Boston SE (8.22(A)) and TEA published the item in Appendix 1.8 of the 2023 answer key, but the excerpt's PDF text layer is too badly damaged by overprinting to transcribe faithfully. The correct selection is recoverable from the key ('history and experience prove that foreign influence is one of the most [harmful enemies] of Republican Government'), and the source is George Washington's Farewell Address, September 19, 1796. Content is outside Boston's era regardless. Re-transcribe from the PDF page image if this item is ever needed.

The 2025 administration tested NO Boston-priority SE with a published-text item. Its two short constructed responses are 8.5(H) (Jackson's plan for American Indians) and 8.23(D) (Spanish influence in the American Southwest); neither is a Boston SE. 2025 also tested no 8.4(A) item at all. All 40 items of 2025 appear in ../item-index.json as metadata.

TEA publishes a full-length Grade 8 Social Studies practice test with complete item text (2023-staar-redesign-8-social-studies-practice-test.pdf), but publishes NO answer key and NO TEKS alignment for it. TEA publishes practice-test answer keys for Math, RLA, Science, Biology, Algebra I, English I and English II, but not for Grade 8 Social Studies. Because there is no official key and no official SE label, these items fail the provenance bar for this dataset and are deliberately NOT captured. Capturing them would mean inventing keys and standard codes, which is the one thing this dataset must never do.
